claims.claim: S3 Options and emitters — options are single-word keys grouped by entity noun with `on` reserved for hooks; a stateful entity owns an `Emitter` by composition with the seven-step pattern and a focused event map.
claims.read: src/server/types.ts:86-141 and patterns.md § Options. Top-level option keys are single words, none encodes grouping through a prefix (no `serverPort`/`databasePath` form), and `on` is not repurposed. I attacked the absence of an emitter directly, because patterns.md § Stateful emitters binds "an entity with lifecycle transitions, constraints, or observable operations": `OllamaProvider` (src/server/OllamaProvider.ts:81-395) holds only immutable configuration in `#` fields, mints every per-call handle inside `generate`/`stream`, and has no lifecycle transition and no state a listener could observe between calls, so the composition pattern has no subject here and AGENTS.md § Design laws "Minimal public API. Add or substantively expand a capability with its first real consumer; do not speculate" forbids adding one. I also attacked grouping `fetch` and `headers` under a `transport` noun, since the package's own prose treats them as one concept; it does not break the rule, because each leaf is already one word and neither encodes a prefix. The guide's promise of a later observability pass is a prose defect filed under S4, not an emitter defect.

claims.claim: S4 Design laws — state is derived rather than stored twice; literal unions represent real domain states; no compatibility shim; mechanism not product policy; no polling architecture; the public API is minimal and every intentional capability is exposed.
claims.read: guides/ollama.md:105 narrates a downstream application's interface decision ("the app enables `think: true` for its thinking model because it DISPLAYS reasoning in the chat's thinking collapsible"), against AGENTS.md § Design laws "Mechanism, not product policy" — finding ollama-subj-8. guides/ollama.md:5, :115 and :237 document a deferred capability ("observability is a later pass", "No events yet", "observability is a separate pass") — finding ollama-subj-9. findings.rule: `AGENTS.md` § Writing: "Write plainly. Say what you mean; mean what you say." and "Do not write aphorisms, metaphors, or rhetorical flourish." `.claude/rules/documentation.md`, opening: "Documentation is an enforced contract, not explanatory decoration." `.claude/rules/writing.md` § Not adopted: "Do not add conversational personality, warmth, or memorability to a reply; the prose stays plain."
findings.wrong: The guide and the TSDoc argue in shouted capitals — `NOT`, `EITHER`, `CLEAN`, `IMPLICIT`, `NEVER`, `AND`, `MAY`, `OWN`, `YOUR`, `THAT`, `LIVE`, `REQUIRES`, `WARMS`, `UNCONDITIONALLY`, `ASSEMBLED`, `AUTHORITATIVE`, `EXPOSE-ONLY`, `CONFIGURABLE`, `DISPLAYS`, `BOUND`, `STACKS`, `CHARS`, `LINES`, `PRIMARY`, `SAME` — so the shipped documentation reads as an argument to a reviewer defending decisions rather than as this package's calm reference, and the emphasis is decoration that carries no instruction a reader can act on. findings.wrong: This package's barrel publishes `joinThinking` and `assembleResult` (helpers.ts:135 and helpers.ts:65) under the exact names its declared runtime dependency `@orkestrel/agent` already publishes for the same two concepts with different signatures (node_modules/@orkestrel/agent/dist/src/core/index.d.ts:3279 `joinThinking(running: string | undefined, next: string): string`, :1012 `assembleResult(outcome: RunOutcome): AgentResult`), and the local `joinThinking` re-implements that dependency's `${running}\n\n${next}` join (dist/src/core/index.js:563) while adding only an empty-string guard on each side — so a consumer importing both barrels, which this package's own guide tells them to do (guides/ollama.md:229), collides on two names.
findings.repair: In `src/server/helpers.ts`, rename `joinThinking` to `buildThinking` and `assembleResult` to `buildResult` (the `build*` prefix .claude/rules/names.md § Standalone helpers fixes for "assembles a composite value from parts"); keep both signatures and both empty-input guards, and have `buildThinking` delegate its non-empty join to `joinThinking` imported from `@orkestrel/agent` so the separator lives in one place. Update the four call sites in `src/server/OllamaProvider.ts` (lines 163, 164, 240, 257), the two `describe` blocks and their titles in `tests/src/server/helpers.test.ts` (lines 4, 10, 66, 120), and the two Surface rows in `guides/ollama.md` (lines 72, 76) plus the sentence naming the leaves at line 81.
consumers: No package in the fleet closure declares @orkestrel/ollama; external consumers importing `joinThinking` or `assembleResult` from '@orkestrel/ollama' must re-point to the new names, so this rides the package's own version bump.

Change a fence, change the transcription beside it."; .claude/rules/documentation.md § Parity: "That proof has a home: `tests/guides.test.ts` executes the flagship fences, per `.claude/rules/tests.md`."
findings.wrong: The file carries only name-resolution parity — surface bijection, method bijection, fence-import resolution, and link resolution — and transcribes no fence, so every value a guide fence claims in a comment (`provider.format // the ContextFormat above` at guides/ollama.md:197, `result.content // 'ok'` at :22, `result.usage // { prompt, completion, total }` at :23) is unproven; nine sibling packages carry the required block (/home/user/fleet/{process,contract,test,mcp,table,lsp,form,codec,probe}/tests/guides.test.ts).
findings.repair: Append a `describe('flagship fences', …)` block to `tests/guides.test.ts` transcribing each hermetically executable fence and asserting the value its comment claims: for the Context-framing fence (guides/ollama.md:184-198) build the same `ContextFormat` literal, call `createOllama` with it, and assert `provider.format` is that object and that `createOllama({ model })` alone leaves `format` undefined; for the Surface fence (guides/ollama.md:13-24) assert the hermetic half its prose claims — that `createOllama({ model })` returns a value whose `name` is `'ollama'` and whose `generate` and `stream` are functions. For the two fences whose comments claim a live model's output (guides/ollama.md:22-23), move the value claim into `tests/service/factories.test.ts` as an executed assertion and change each fence comment to name the shape rather than a literal answer, so no unproven value remains under a fence. Import `createOllama` from `@src/server` in tests/guides.test.ts; the `guides` project runs in Node with the browser disabled, so no new setup file is needed.

findings.rule: .claude/rules/tests.md § Test contract: "Measure an elapsed interval with `performance.now()`, never `Date.now()`. `Date.now()` returns whole milliseconds, so an interval built from two of its readings truncates at both ends and can under-report by a millisecond — enough to fail a boundary assertion against a timer that behaved correctly. `performance.now()` is monotonic and sub-millisecond, and it does not move when the wall clock does."
findings.wrong: The self-calibrating deadline test builds two elapsed intervals from five `Date.now()` readings (lines 356, 364, 367, 368, 373) — `window = ended - first` and `deadline = first - started + window / 2` — and puts the first straight into a boundary assertion (`expect(window).toBeGreaterThan(250)`, line 379) and the second into the provider's `timeout` option (line 385), which is exactly the truncating, wall-clock-sensitive measurement the rule names.
findings.repair: In `tests/service/OllamaProvider.test.ts`, replace `Date.now()` with `performance.now()` at lines 356, 364, 367, 368, and 373. Leave `Math.round` at line 380, which already converts the sub-millisecond reading to the whole-millisecond `timeout` the provider takes.

findings.rule: .claude/rules/tests.md § Shared test infrastructure: "Export every reusable helper, fixture type, factory, constant, and guard from setup files."; .claude/rules/architecture.md § Declaration placement: "Every declaration in a centralized file is exported. Fold away a trivial single-use declaration or export/test it; never leave it hidden."
findings.wrong: `FILLER_SENTENCE` is a module-scope constant in a setup file that is not exported, so the deterministic filler text `fillWorkspace` writes is unreachable to the tests that assert on the files it produced — and the fleet policy sweep cannot report it, because its export population is `{app,src}/**` only (tests/setupPolicy.ts:229).
findings.repair: In `tests/setup.ts`, add `export` to `FILLER_SENTENCE` at line 100 and give it a TSDoc line: `/** The fixed sentence {@link fillWorkspace} repeats to fill each generated document. */`. In `tests/setup.test.ts`, add one case to the existing `fillWorkspace` describe asserting that a written document's text starts with `FILLER_SENTENCE`, so the newly exported constant is proved rather than merely exposed.

The project that requires the daemon is `service`, which vite.config.ts:130-142 declares and which `test` never runs.
